title: A clear offer and next action

sections.skill: Write a clear offer and a single call to action

questions.prompt: Which three questions should the top of a main page answer?

choices.text: When the owner was born, where she grew up, and her hobbies
What, who it is for, and what to do next
How big the company hopes to grow over the next ten years
Which web host and font the site uses for its pages

questions.correct_answer: What, who it is for, and what to do next
questions.intro: A visitor decides in seconds whether a website is useful. The top of the main page should answer three questions: WHAT do you offer, WHO is it for, and WHAT should the visitor do next? The next action is called a CALL TO ACTION, such as "Book a free 15-minute call" or "Order now." Use one main call to action per page, in plain words, easy to see. Example: "Dog walking for busy owners in Eastfield. Book your first walk." Vague slogans like "Excellence in everything" do not tell visitors what to do.

sections.skill: A shop sign and an open door

questions.prompt: A website's top section is like what?

choices.text: The parking lot behind the shop

questions.intro: Walking past a shop, you look for a sign saying what it sells and an open door. "Fresh bread, open now" tells you everything; a sign reading "Dreams" does not. A website's top section is the sign, and the call to action is the open door. If either is missing, people walk past, even if the shop is good.

A locked gate around the shop
